name: Favourite-longshot harvesting: systematic longshot selling / NO buying, conditioned on category
one_line: Rest NO bids against 2-15c YES in many-candidate non-sports events and hold to resolution; the bias is large for the buyers (19c per dollar) but the seller's harvest is 2-3% per position over weeks, negative per dollar in the big markets, and concentrated where disputes and insiders live.
maturity: Emerging (bias Established on 588M Polymarket and 72M Kalshi trades; harvest unproven): own replay finds +2.0-2.6% per NO position (event-clustered CI above zero) but -1.8% per dollar; no attributable Polymarket strategy PnL; the taker always-NO version is priced in
requires_ai: no; base-rate table and event clustering; optional LLM rules screen
edge: Lottery demand, rebate-subsidised churn and a decaying risk premium paid by YES takers
capital: $1k-$10k to run, $10k+ to matter; NO at 0.92 locks 92c for weeks at 0% yield
build_time: 2-3 weeks solo on an LP or bond-carry stack; 5-7 weeks from scratch
opportunity_size: ~$96k/day of taker YES buying in the 80 most active longshot markets; transferable pool ~$6-18k/day across all makers; shrinking per dollar
expected_results: no verified PnL; replay +2.6%/position at 30 days (CI +1.3 to +3.8), -1.8% per dollar; guess $5k earns +$25-55/month
competition: Median 32 makers per market; always-NO bots crowd the taker side
flag: none; grey data licence only if incorporated
validate: Event-clustered replay at historical asks by category and field size, then a 90-day paper book and $2k maker-only pilot
top_risk: Correlated hits in disputed or insider-driven geopolitics longshots
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to build and reusable as an overlay on files 02, 14 and 23, but as a standalone book it earns tens of dollars a month per $5k, locks capital at zero yield, and the dollar-weighted edge is negative in exactly the liquid markets a solo maker can fill in.
speed_class: execution-sensitive: base-rate carry over weeks, but a crossed 3.7c spread or a stale ask at a shock is the year's edge
results_1k: marginal; +$0 to +$8/month net, 10th percentile -$70 (derived Monte Carlo)
min_capital: ~$3k; 30 positions of $100 with a 4% per-event cap
capacity_ceiling: ~$50-100k solo; ~10% of a market's daily YES-taker flow
changes_made: Written 2026-09-28 with live checks: full text of arXiv 2609.12878 (tables 6-10, 14, 15), Becker's Kalshi page and SSRN abstract, CESifo and Krause abstracts via Crossref, Yang's risk-premium abstract, the Nothing Ever Happens repo, README, HN thread, Decrypt/Yahoo and Protos pieces, Polymarket's accuracy page, fee, maker-rebate, taker-rebate, liquidity-reward and changelog docs.

Own Gamma keyset census of 213,854 active markets (17,363 non-sports sub-15c markets; 7,050 in the tradable 2-15c band within 180 days), CLOB books on the 14 most active, Data API taker tape on the 80 most active (taker YES buying ~$96k/day vs taker NO buying ~$631k/day; median YES ticket $7.6; 48% of YES-taker dollars in $500+ tickets).

Own leakage-controlled replay of 6,703 resolved 2026 markets: NO on 2-15c YES +2.6% per position at 30 days (event-clustered CI +1.3 to +3.8), +2.8% per event, -1.8% per dollar; politics +1.0%; finance and economics negative; neg-risk rungs -0.4% vs +3.7% standalone; naive 35-65c NO rule +24.9% per market and -15.4% per dollar.

Corrected the brief's framing: the maturity hypothesis 'Emerging' is kept, but the maker-side 'Established' candidate label is rejected (no attributable PnL); the Gamma offset endpoint caps limit at 100 and refuses offsets above ~2,000, keyset pagination needs after_cursor; the accuracy page's NO share is now 77.8%, not 73.3%.

Table 15 of the paper (returns by number of child markets) used to add the 'never sell longshots in 2-5-child events' rule; the taker-rebate wV formula shown to subsidise longshot YES buying 19x per dollar versus NO buying.

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-28 (25 sources re-fetched, all reachable; SSRN abstract pages 403 but Crossref records confirm; replay report reproduced exactly from the saved records; flow tape re-run on the top 20 markets; Gamma offset/keyset limits re-tested): corrected the 1-day replay figure (+0.66%, CI spanning zero, not +1.5%); the volume split (>$100k) relabelled diagnostic because it uses final volume, which is unknown at entry; neg-risk cut dated to the 7-day horizon; disclosed that 48% of the band and 70% of the sample are keyword-categorised (pre-feeType) and that the 'clean' subset dropped 2,271 untagged game/team/'win' titles including 2025 election-winner fields; Monte Carlo for the size table re-run with the stated 45-day lock (gross = deployed x edge x 0.67), which cut the $1k/$5k/$10k nets to +$0-8 / +$25-55 / +$50-115 and made the 10th percentiles negative (-$70 / -$150 / -$200); stated that the replay is an upper bound for a maker whose fills are adverse-selected; accuracy-page note fixed (embedded data: 510,717 No / 145,500 Yes = 656,217 resolved markets; the '94.2% one week / 96.4% one day' figures were SVG coordinates, removed); Q1 2026 paper wording aligned with Appendix B; Becker page date and SSRN publication date, Dubach v2 date added.
open_doubts: The replay uses mids and 12-hour price buckets and fills the passive buyer in every market; at historical asks and with adverse selection on resting bids the per-position edge would be lower than +2.6%.

The replay sample is March-April 2026 heavy (first 9,000 candidates by id), 70% of it predates the feeType field and is categorised by title keyword, and the 'clean' subset was produced by a keyword rule that also removed 2025 election-winner fields; a full-year, fee-type-tagged replay could move the category numbers.
The volume split in step 2 is not a tradable filter: it uses final volume, and low-volume markets never hit in the sample partly because volume accrues when something happens.
No Polymarket wallet with attributable longshot-selling PnL was found; the maker-side evidence is inferential (winners are limit-order providers; Kalshi makers +1.12%).

The paper's pooled longshot loss (-19.35%) has a confidence interval spanning zero and flips sign under equal-event weighting; which weighting describes a seller's realised PnL depends on where the seller's fills concentrate.

Taker-tape statistics come from the last 500 taker trades per market (takerOnly default), so the $/day figures are short-window snapshots (re-run on the top 20 reproduced them), and large YES tickets may be hedges rather than informed flow.
The size-table Monte Carlo assumes hits shared in pairs; with wider event correlation (a war, a court ruling) the 10th percentiles are worse than shown.
E4's Kalshi maker/taker loss figures (-10% / -32%) are snippet-only and were not re-verified.
